title: 14-Day Patagonia Itinerary: Torres del Paine, Perito Moreno, Fitz Roy, and the End of the World
description: Two weeks exploring the wildest corners of Argentina and Chile — from the thundering ice walls of Perito Moreno to the granite spires of Fitz Roy, the legendary W Trek in Torres del Paine, and the southernmost city on earth.

days.title: Arrival in Buenos Aires
days.description: Fly into Buenos Aires and soak in the capital energy before heading south. Settle into San Telmo or Palermo. Walk La Boca colorful streets and eat the best steak of your life.

activities.name: Arrive and Settle In
activities.description: Land at Ezeiza Airport (EZE) and transfer to your hotel in Palermo or San Telmo. Both are walkable, full of character, with great food.
details: Remis (private car) from airport is safest — book through your hotel
Get Argentine pesos from Banelco ATMs — avoid airport exchange kiosks

activities.name: Explore San Telmo
activities.description: Walk the cobblestone streets — Buenos Aires oldest neighborhood. Browse antique shops, watch street tango dancers, and grab a cafe cortado.
details: If it is Sunday, the San Telmo antiques market on Calle Defensa is unmissable
La Boca Caminito is 15 min south — colorful but stick to the tourist area
tips: The parallel exchange rate in Argentina can save you 20-30%. Ask locals about the dolar blue rate before exchanging money.

days.title: Buenos Aires to El Calafate
days.description: Morning flight south to El Calafate, gateway to Los Glaciares National Park. Walk the lakefront, browse gear shops, and fuel up with your first cordero al asador.

activities.name: Fly to Patagonia
activities.description: Catch the early flight from Aeroparque (AEP) to El Calafate (FTE) — about 3 hours. The descent reveals the vast steppe and turquoise Lago Argentino.
details: Book flights early — Aerolineas Argentinas has the best domestic routes
Pack layers in your carry-on — El Calafate can be 15C colder than Buenos Aires

activities.name: Explore El Calafate
activities.description: Walk Avenida del Libertador along the lake — shops, chocolate stores, and restaurants. Visit the Glaciarium museum for glacier science and an ice bar.
details: Glaciarium is 6 km from town — taxis are cheap
Rent any missing gear here — crampons, poles, and waterproofs available
tips: El Calafate is windy year-round. Even on sunny days, a windproof layer is essential.

days.title: Perito Moreno Glacier
days.description: One of the only advancing glaciers in the world — a 5-km-wide, 60-meter-tall wall of ice that regularly calves massive chunks into Lago Argentino with thunderous cracks.

activities.name: Drive to the Glacier
activities.description: Depart El Calafate for Perito Moreno (80 km, about 1.5 hours). Walk the extensive boardwalk system — multiple levels and viewpoints.
details: Park entrance fee is separate — cards accepted at the gate
Bring sunscreen and sunglasses — ice reflects UV intensely

activities.name: Big Ice or Mini Trekking (Optional)
activities.description: Strap on crampons and walk ON the glacier. Big Ice (3.5 hours) goes deep; Mini Trekking (1.5 hours) is a shorter taster. Both by Hielo and Aventura.
details: Big Ice must be booked well in advance — sells out fast
They provide crampons — just bring warm layers and gloves

activities.name: Boardwalk Exploration
activities.description: Spend the afternoon at different viewpoints. Calving is random but more frequent on warm afternoons — the crack of ice breaking echoes across the lake.
details: Best calving views from the lower boardwalks — closer to the ice face
Bring packed lunch — limited food options at the park
tips: Glacier calving comes down to luck. Be patient and keep your camera ready — the crack sound gives you a 2-second warning.

days.title: El Calafate to El Chalten
days.description: North to El Chalten, Argentina trekking capital. The 3-hour bus follows Route 40 through vast steppe. On a clear day, Fitz Roy appears long before you arrive.

activities.name: Bus to El Chalten
activities.description: Take the 8 AM bus (about 3 hours). Route 40 through Patagonian steppe — endless grasslands, guanacos, massive skies. Watch for Fitz Roy on the horizon.
details: Book the first bus to maximize your afternoon
Sit on the left for the best Fitz Roy views approaching town

activities.name: Warm-Up Hike
activities.description: After checking in, hike to Chorrillo del Salto — a 20m waterfall in lenga forest, 1 hour round trip. All trailheads start from town — no car needed.
details: Rent trekking poles at Viento Oeste if needed
Buy trail snacks at the small supermarket — limited selection
Check park ranger weather board at the bus station
tips: Weather in El Chalten changes by the hour. The park rangers update the forecast daily — check it every morning before choosing your hike.

days.neighborhoods: Monte Fitz Roy . Laguna de los Tres
days.title: Laguna de los Tres (Fitz Roy)
days.description: The crown jewel. 25-km round trip through lenga forests to Monte Fitz Roy, where Laguna de los Tres sits in a glacial cirque at 1,170m. One of the greatest mountain views on earth.

activities.name: Start the Fitz Roy Trek
activities.description: Begin at 6 AM from the trailhead. First 3 hours through lenga forests along the Rio Blanco. Well-marked and moderate until the final push.
details: Start before 7 AM — trail gets crowded, afternoon clouds roll in
Bring 2+ liters of water, snacks, warm layers, rain gear

activities.name: The Final Ascent
activities.description: The last kilometer is a brutal 400m vertical scramble on loose scree. At the top, Laguna de los Tres — turquoise glacial lake with Fitz Roy 3,405m granite spires towering above. The Patagonia poster shot.
details: Trekking poles help enormously on the scree section
Clear skies are rare — if you get them, you are incredibly lucky

activities.name: Laguna Sucia and Descent
activities.description: On the way down, detour to Laguna Sucia — rated 9/10 by experienced hikers, equally stunning with far fewer people. Continue via Laguna Capri for Fitz Roy reflections.
details: Laguna Sucia is a must — different dramatic angle on Fitz Roy
tips: 9-10 hour hike, 25 km, 800m elevation gain. Start early, go at your own pace, and do not skip Laguna Sucia on the way down.

days.title: Laguna Torre and Cerro Torre
days.description: Hike to the base of Cerro Torre, a granite needle considered one of the hardest summits in the world. The 18-km trail is gentler than yesterday, with icebergs floating in the lagoon.

activities.name: Trek to Laguna Torre
activities.description: Depart 7:30 AM from the trailhead. The 9-km trail is flatter and more forgiving — perfect for tired legs. Icebergs float in the glacial lagoon with Cerro Torre needle rising behind.
details: Wind at Laguna Torre can be extreme — windproof layer essential
Glacial water from river crossings is safe to drink

activities.name: Mirador Maestri and Picnic
activities.description: Continue past the lagoon to Mirador Maestri (30 min) for an elevated panorama above the icebergs and glacier. Picnic lunch by the lagoon with a postcard view.
details: Mirador Maestri is a short but worthwhile extension — do not skip it

days.title: Rest Day or Lago del Desierto
days.description: After two big hiking days, choose your adventure. Rest in town or day trip to Lago del Desierto — a pristine glacial lake 37 km north with kayaking and hidden glaciers.

activities.name: Option A: Rest and Recover
activities.description: Sleep in, linger over pastries at Domo Blanco (the best bakery in town), browse the craft market, visit the mountaineering museum. Shuttle to Lago del Desierto (1 hour, about $30 USD round trip). This pristine lake was disputed between Argentina and Chile until 1994. Short hike to Glaciar Huemul viewpoint, optional kayaking.
details: Domo Blanco sells out by noon — go early
Book shuttle at any hostel or tour agency
Kayaking available at the dock

days.title: El Chalten to Puerto Natales
days.description: Big transit day crossing from Argentina into Chile. Patagonian steppe scenery is hauntingly beautiful — endless grasslands, guanacos, condors. Puerto Natales is a cozy harbor town on Last Hope Sound.

activities.name: Bus to El Calafate
activities.description: Take the 7:30 AM bus back to El Calafate (about 3 hours). Quick lunch in town before the afternoon connection.
details: Buses Pacheco and Cootra are the most reliable

activities.name: Cross into Chile
activities.description: Bus from El Calafate to Puerto Natales (about 5 hours including Cerro Castillo border crossing). Have passport ready — immigration is quick but can take 30-60 min in peak season.
details: Have your passport ready — Argentine exit and Chilean entry
Puerto Natales shops close early — stock up at UNIMARC before 8 PM

activities.name: Sunset on Last Hope Sound
activities.description: Walk the Puerto Natales waterfront at sunset — the light on Last Hope Sound is magical. Small, charming, walkable, and the base for Torres del Paine.
tips: If doing the W Trek, buy all food at UNIMARC tonight. Only decent supermarket, and options inside the park are expensive.

days.title: W Trek Day 1 — Base Torres
days.description: Enter Torres del Paine National Park. Start the W Trek with its defining hike — 22 km round trip to the iconic Base Torres viewpoint. Three granite towers above turquoise lake.

activities.name: Enter Torres del Paine
activities.description: Take the 6:30 AM bus from Puerto Natales (about 2 hours). Register at Laguna Amarga entrance, pay park fee (~$40 USD). Transfer to Hotel Las Torres.
details: Park entrance ~$40 USD for foreigners — cash or card
Book refugios MONTHS in advance — they sell out

activities.name: Hike to Mirador Base Torres
activities.description: 22-km round trip, about 9 hours. Hike through forests and rivers to Refugio Chileno (halfway rest), then the steep final scramble. Three massive granite towers above a turquoise glacial lake — the iconic image of Patagonia.
details: Final scramble is steep and rocky — trekking poles essential
Start early — afternoon clouds often obscure the towers
Overnight at Hotel Las Torres, Camp Central, or Refugio Chileno
tips: This itinerary does a streamlined 3-day W Trek hitting the three main viewpoints from refugio bases. More flexible, less gear needed.

days.title: W Trek Day 2 — French Valley
days.description: Many hikers' favorite day. Trek along the Cuernos del Paine, then enter the French Valley — a hanging valley surrounded by glaciers, waterfalls, and sheer rock walls.

activities.name: Into the French Valley
activities.description: Depart from Refugio Los Cuernos and trek to Campamento Italiano. Leave your heavy pack and travel light into the French Valley — a cathedral of granite, ice, and waterfalls. The valley is wind-protected, making it one of the best hiking days in Patagonia.
details: Leave your main pack at Campamento Italiano
Refugio Los Cuernos has hot meals and wine

activities.name: Mirador Britanico
activities.description: The steep 2-hour climb to Mirador Britanico is absolutely worth it. At the top, a 360-degree panorama of the entire Paine massif — towers, glaciers, lakes — spreads in every direction. Have lunch and take it all in.
details: This is the single best viewpoint in Torres del Paine
The climb is steep but the valley shelters you from wind

activities.name: Continue to Paine Grande
activities.description: Descend from the French Valley and continue west along the lake to Refugio Paine Grande — the major hub of the W Trek and departure point for the catamaran.
tips: The French Valley is often called the highlight of the entire W Trek — and for good reason. If you only have clear weather for one day, pray it's this one.

days.title: W Trek Day 3 — Grey Glacier
days.description: Final arm of the W along Lago Grey to Grey Glacier — a massive river of ice from the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Icebergs in every shade of blue.

activities.name: Trek to Grey Glacier
activities.description: Depart Refugio Paine Grande toward Grey Glacier. The trail hugs the shore of Lago Grey, passing icebergs in surreal shades of blue. At the viewpoint, the full face of Grey Glacier stretches before you.
details: Big Foot Patagonia is the only ice hiking operator — max 5 per guide, book ahead
Grey Glacier ice hike costs about a third of similar in Argentina

activities.name: Ice Hiking on Grey Glacier (Optional)
activities.description: If you booked in advance with Big Foot Patagonia, spend 3 hours walking on the glacier through crevasses, ice caves, and frozen rivers. This was rated 10/10 by travelers and is one of the most memorable activities in all of Patagonia.
details: Only 5 spots per guide — book as early as possible
They provide crampons and gear; bring warm gloves and layers

activities.name: Catamaran Across Lago Pehoe
activities.description: Return to Refugio Paine Grande and catch the catamaran across Lago Pehoe to Pudeto. The crossing is spectacular — the Paine massif towers above turquoise water. Connect to the bus back to Puerto Natales.
details: Catamaran has fixed departure times — check schedule and do not miss it
Hosteria Pehoe has one of Patagonia's best views if you want to splurge on a night
tips: The W Trek is complete! Three days of the most spectacular mountain scenery on earth. Celebrate with a hot shower and cold beer in Puerto Natales tonight.

days.title: Puerto Natales Recovery Day
days.description: Your legs earned this. Sleep in, explore Puerto Natales, and eat everything. Optional Balmaceda and Serrano glaciers boat trip for a relaxed day on the water.

activities.name: Late Start & Explore
activities.description: Sleep in. Walk to Cafe Kaiken for a late breakfast, then visit the Museo Historico for the story of Patagonian settlement — from indigenous peoples to European pioneers. Walk the waterfront where dolphins sometimes appear in Last Hope Sound.
details: Sunset on the waterfront is stunning — don't miss it
Laundry services available in town — refresh clothes before Ushuaia

activities.name: Optional: Balmaceda & Serrano Glaciers Boat Trip
activities.description: A relaxed full-day boat trip through Bernardo O'Higgins National Park to see the Balmaceda and Serrano glaciers. The scenery is lush and green — a nice contrast to the stark beauty of Torres del Paine. Spot seals and waterfalls along the way.
details: Rated 7/10 — scenic but not as dramatic as Grey or Perito Moreno
Good option if you want more glaciers without hiking
tips: Puerto Natales is small but charming. The local wool shops have beautiful handmade guanaco and sheep wool products — great souvenirs.

days.title: Fly to Ushuaia — End of the World
days.description: Fly from Punta Arenas to Ushuaia, the southernmost city in the world. Nestled between the Martial Mountains and the Beagle Channel, Ushuaia feels like the edge of civilization.

activities.name: Transit to Ushuaia
activities.description: Bus from Puerto Natales to Punta Arenas (about 3 hours), then fly to Ushuaia (about 1 hour). The approach into Ushuaia is dramatic — mountains plunge into the Beagle Channel as the city appears below.
details: Book the Punta Arenas-Ushuaia flight in advance — limited daily flights
Ushuaia is a tax-free zone — electronics and outdoor gear are cheaper here

activities.name: Explore Ushuaia & Martial Glacier
activities.description: Walk the waterfront and harbor — fishing boats and expedition ships bound for Antarctica line the docks. Visit the Museo del Fin del Mundo (End of the World Museum), then hike to the Martial Glacier viewpoint for sweeping views over the city and Beagle Channel.
details: The Martial Glacier trail is accessible by taxi or shuttle from town
The museum is small but interesting — history of Tierra del Fuego and its indigenous peoples

days.neighborhoods: Tierra del Fuego NP · Beagle Channel · Isla Martillo
days.title: Tierra del Fuego & Beagle Channel
days.description: Your final day in Patagonia. Morning in Tierra del Fuego National Park at the end of the Pan-American Highway. Afternoon Beagle Channel cruise past sea lions, cormorants, and the iconic Les Eclaireurs lighthouse.

activities.name: Tierra del Fuego National Park
activities.description: Hike the Costera Trail to Bahia Lapataia — the official end of Route 3, the Pan-American Highway that stretches from Alaska to here. Take the obligatory photo at the End of Route 3 sign. Continue to Hito XXIV trail along Lago Roca to the Chilean border marker.
details: The End of the World Train is touristy but fun — rides through the national park
The park has beautiful sub-Antarctic forest, beavers dams, and dramatic coastline

activities.name: Beagle Channel Cruise
activities.description: Board a catamaran for a Beagle Channel cruise — past Isla de los Lobos (sea lions), Isla de los Pajaros (cormorants), and the iconic Les Eclaireurs lighthouse (often mistakenly called the End of the World lighthouse). If it's penguin season (Oct-Mar), add a stop at Isla Martillo to see Magellanic and Gentoo penguins nesting on the shore.
details: Book the longer cruise route that includes the penguin colony
Penguin season runs October through March
Dress warmly — the channel is windy and cold even in summer

activities.name: Final Dinner at the End of the World
activities.description: Your last night in Patagonia. Reflect on 14 days of glaciers, granite spires, and windswept wilderness over one final feast.
tips: If flying out tomorrow, the airport is just 4 km from the city center. Most flights connect through Buenos Aires — consider a layover day in BA if you have time.
